page: Microsoft Azure D160as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 family, powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server features 160 vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 640.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the D160as_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests. Memory performance is similarly robust, with cached read-only bandwidth reaching 14,657.53 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 209.97 GB/sec. The processor's support for advanced vector extensions (AVX-512) and cryptography instructions drives high-throughput operations, as evidenced by top-tier scores in Passmark CPU encryption, database operations, and Redis SET benchmarks, which reached 200.12 million operations per second.

Given its massive compute density and balanced memory configuration, this server is highly efficient for resource-intensive enterprise workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, and CPU-based large language model (LLM) inference, where it achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a design tradeoff that optimizes cost efficiency for pure compute and memory-bound workloads.
